claim: 597 genes were induced by LPS >1.5 fold at FDR < 0.1 in primary mouse bone-marrow-derived macrophages (BMDM) treated for 1 hr compared to vehicle-treated BMDM
source: At FDR < 0.1 we found that, compared to vehicle-treated BMDM, 597 genes were induced by LPS >1.5 fold.
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq experimental data from BMDM treated with LPS for 1 hr

claim: Of 597 LPS-induced genes, the induction of 201 genes was attenuated >1.3 fold by Dex co-treatment
source: Of these, the induction of 201 genes was attenuated >1.3 fold by Dex co-treatment (Figure 1A and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data comparing LPS vs LPS+Dex treatment shown in Figure 1A

claim: Acutely GR-repressed genes are predominantly involved in cytokine signaling
source: As expected, GO analysis of acutely GR-repressed genes revealed predominantly those involved in cytokine signaling (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by Gene Ontology analysis of the 201 Dex-repressed genes shown in Figure 1A

claim: Following LPS + Dex exposure, 9987 GR peaks were detected in BMDM
source: Following LPS + Dex exposure, we detected 9987 GR peaks (union of two replicates)
evidence: The claim is supported by GR ChIP-seq data from BMDM treated with LPS + Dex for 45 min

claim: 5397 (54.1%) of GR peaks did not overlap with p65 peaks under LPS + Dex conditions
source: 5397 (54.1%) of which did not overlap with p65 peaks at the same conditions (Figure 1B, top, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq overlap analysis shown in Figure 1B

claim: GR unique peaks in LPS + Dex treated BMDM show predominance of centrally enriched NR3C-binding motifs, ETS family member motifs, and AP1 family member motifs
source: Motif overrepresentation analysis in these GR unique peaks revealed predominance of centrally enriched NR3C-binding motifs, which represent GREs and highly related NR-binding sites, those for ETS family members, such as the macrophage lineage-determining TF SPI1 (PU.1 and SPIB), and AP1 family members (Figure 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B, left panel).
evidence: The claim is supported by motif overrepresentation analysis using MEME-ChIP on GR unique peaks shown in Figure 1B

claim: 7052 p65 peaks were detected after LPS + Dex treatment in BMDM
source: The analysis of p65 binding after LPS + Dex treatment revealed 7052 peaks (union of two replicates)
evidence: The claim is supported by p65 ChIP-seq data from BMDM treated with LPS + Dex for 45 min

claim: 2344 (33.8%) of p65 peaks were uniquely bound by p65 under LPS + Dex conditions
source: of which 2344 (33.8%) were uniquely bound by p65 (Figure 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The claim is supported by p65 ChIP-seq peak analysis shown in Figure 1B

claim: p65 unique peaks show enrichment of NF-kB/Rela binding motifs, ETS motifs, and AP1 motifs
source: Motif analysis indicated an enrichment of NF-kB/Rela binding motifs, as well as ETS and AP1 motifs (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by motif analysis of p65 unique peaks shown in Figure 1B

claim: The GR and p65 cistromes shared 4589 peaks under LPS + Dex conditions
source: Importantly, the GR and p65 cistromes shared 4589 peaks, which corresponds to nearly half of all GR- and 2/3 of all p65-binding peaks.
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq overlap analysis of GR and p65 peaks

claim: Overlapping GR and p65 peaks show predominance for NR3C/GRE, ETS family, NF-kB/Rela and AP1 binding motifs enriched near peak summits
source: Motif analysis of these peaks showed a predominance for NR3C/GRE, ETS family, NF-kB/Rela and AP1 binding motifs that were enriched near the peak summits (Figure 1B, bottom, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B, middle panel).
evidence: The claim is supported by motif analysis of overlapping GR and p65 peaks shown in Figure 1B

claim: In Dex-treated BMDM, GR-binding sites formed 3377 peaks
source: In Dex-treated BMDM, GR-binding sites formed 3377 peaks.
evidence: The claim is supported by GR ChIP-seq data from BMDM treated with Dex only for 45 min

claim: 3165 GR peaks in Dex-treated BMDM also appeared in the GR LPS + Dex cistrome
source: Of those, 3165 also appeared in the GR LPS + Dex cistrome (with only 212 peaks unique to Dex-treated BMDM)
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of GR ChIP-seq peaks between Dex and LPS+Dex conditions

claim: 6817 GR peaks were gained in the GR LPS + Dex cistrome compared to Dex alone
source: whereas 6817 were gained in the GR LPS + Dex cistrome (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, right panel).
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of GR ChIP-seq peaks shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A

claim: ETS and NR3C-binding motifs are over-represented in both Dex-unique and Dex-LPS+Dex shared subsets of GR peaks
source: ETS and NR3C-binding motifs were over-represented in both Dex-unique and Dex – LPS + Dex shared subsets of GR peaks and trended toward the peak summit (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1B, right panel).
evidence: The claim is supported by motif analysis shown in Figure 1C

claim: NF-kB/Rela motif enrichment was not detected in Dex-unique and Dex-LPS+Dex shared subsets of GR-binding peaks
source: We did not detect NF-kB/Rela motif enrichment in these two subsets of GR-binding peaks.
evidence: The claim is supported by motif analysis of GR peaks

claim: Among 6817 peaks unique to the GR LPS + Dex cistrome, there is overrepresentation of NF-kB and AP1 motifs while NR3C motifs are no longer enriched
source: However, among 6817 peaks unique to the GR LPS + Dex cistrome we readily observed an overrepresentation of NF-kB and AP1 motifs while NR3C motifs were no longer enriched (Figure 1C, compare top/middle vs. bottom motif enrichment panels)
evidence: The claim is supported by motif analysis shown in Figure 1C

claim: Inflammatory signaling and p65/NF-kB activation drives GR recruitment to sites specifically under repressing LPS + Dex conditions
source: indicating that inflammatory signaling and p65/NF-kB activation was driving GR recruitment to such sites specifically under repressing LPS + Dex conditions.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the motif enrichment patterns showing NF-kB motifs in LPS+Dex unique GR peaks

claim: The majority of GR and p65-binding sites are located in distal intergenic (~39–47% of peaks) and intronic (~40% on average) regions
source: The majority of GR and p65-binding sites were located in distal intergenic (~39–47% of peaks) and intronic (~40% on average) regions (Figure 1D)
evidence: The claim is supported by genomic location analysis of ChIP-seq peaks shown in Figure 1D

claim: GR and p65 binding patterns in macrophages are similar to previously reported GR and p65 cistromes in various cell lines
source: similar to previously reported GR and p65 cistromes in various cell lines (Reddy et al., 2009; Barish et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison to published literature

claim: Among 201 LPS-induced Dex-repressed genes, approximately 52% of GR-binding peaks are located in distal intergenic regions
source: In this subset, a somewhat larger fraction (~52%, compared to 39–47% genome-wide) of GR-binding peaks were located in distal intergenic regions
evidence: The claim is supported by analysis of GR peak locations near Dex-repressed genes

claim: Among 201 LPS-induced Dex-repressed genes, the fraction of GR peaks in introns dropped from 40% to 24% compared to whole-genome GR cistrome
source: whereas the fraction of peaks in the introns dropped from 40% to 24% compared to whole-genome GR cistrome (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is supported by genomic location analysis shown in Figure 1D

claim: The shift in GR peak distribution at Dex-repressed genes was not due to a preponderance of shorter introns or genes in the Dex-repressed subset
source: This shift was not due to a preponderance of shorter introns or genes in Dex-repressed subset (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by gene and intron length distribution analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C

claim: Among the 201 Dex-repressed genes, 81% of GR binding sites are unique to the LPS + Dex condition compared to 68% genome-wide
source: Comparison of GR binding near the 201 Dex-repressed genes with an entire GR cistrome shows that a greater fraction of binding sites was unique to the LPS + Dex condition (81% vs. 68%, Figure 1E)
evidence: The claim is supported by GR binding site analysis shown in Figure 1E

claim: At GR-sensitive genes, GR binding occurs at sites matching those of p65, but only in LPS + Dex and not LPS- or Dex-alone treated BMDM
source: Several representative examples of GR and p65 co-binding near GR-sensitive genes are shown in Figure 1F: at each gene, GR binding occurred at sites matching those of p65, but only in LPS + Dex and not LPS- or Dex-alone treated BMDM.
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq read density profiles shown in Figure 1F

claim: LPS-dependent p65 binding fully persists in the presence of Dex
source: Importantly, LPS-dependent p65 binding fully persisted in the presence of Dex.
evidence: The claim is supported by p65 ChIP-seq data comparing LPS and LPS+Dex conditions

claim: The total number of p65 binding peaks in the presence of LPS and LPS + Dex is comparable both genome-wide and in the vicinity of GR-repressed genes
source: In fact, the total number of p65 binding peaks in the presence of LPS and LPS + Dex was comparable both genome-wide, and in the vicinity of our GR-repressed genes (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A, right and 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by p65 ChIP-seq peak analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2A and 2B

claim: Approximately 2/3 of the LPS-induced p65 peaks persist in LPS + Dex-treated BMDM
source: In each case, ~2/3 of the LPS-induced p65 peaks persisted in LPS + Dex-treated BMDM.
evidence: The claim is supported by p65 ChIP-seq peak overlap analysis

claim: Among p65 LPS + Dex peaks functionally constrained to Dex-repressed genes, 80% overlap LPS-induced peaks
source: Moreover, among p65 LPS + Dex peaks functionally constrained to Dex-repressed genes, 80% (up from 68% genome-wide) overlapped LPS-induced peaks (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: The claim is supported by p65 peak overlap analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2C

claim: Of the 201 genes repressed by Dex in the context of LPS-mediated macrophage activation, only 56 were repressed ≥1.3 fold upon treatment with Dex alone
source: Interestingly, of the 201 genes repressed by Dex in the context of LPS-mediated macrophage activation, only 56 were repressed ≥1.3 fold (and only 16 of those ≥2 fold) upon treatment with Dex alone (Supplementary file 1; RNA-seq dataset from [Chinenov et al., 2014])
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data analysis comparing Dex effects in LPS-activated vs unstimulated macrophages

claim: NF-kB activation is required for GR recruitment to the majority of Dex-sensitive genes
source: further supporting a requirement for NF-kB activation for GR recruitment to the majority of genes Dex-sensitive genes.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that most Dex-sensitive genes require LPS for GR-mediated repression

claim: p65 is a central component of repression complexes in GC-treated BMDM
source: Combined, these results further corroborate a tethering model in which p65 is a central component of repression complexes in GC-treated BMDM.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the extensive co-localization of GR and p65 and the requirement for NF-kB activation

claim: At several pro-inflammatory genes in unstimulated BMDM, promoter-proximally paused Pol 2 is in a complex with NELF and enters productive elongation following LPS treatment
source: We have reported that at several pro-inflammatory genes in unstimulated BMDM, promoter-proximally paused Pol 2 is in a complex with NELF and enters productive elongation following LPS treatment (Adelman et al., 2009; Gupte et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by previous publications from the authors' group

claim: Tnf, Hilpda and Btg2 display accumulation of Pol 2 near the TSS in untreated BMDM
source: Of those, Tnf, Hilpda and Btg2, all display accumulation of Pol 2 near the TSS in untreated BMDM.
evidence: The claim is supported by Pol 2 ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 2A

claim: Upon 45-min LPS treatment, Tnf, Hilpda and Btg2 show additional Pol 2 loading and redistribution into the body of the gene
source: Upon a 45-min LPS treatment, we detect additional Pol 2 loading and, notably, its redistribution into the body of the gene
evidence: The claim is supported by Pol 2 ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 2A

claim: Upon LPS + Dex treatment, Pol 2 at Tnf, Hilpda and Btg2 largely remains near the TSS resembling a 'paused' pattern seen in unstimulated BMDM
source: conversely, upon LPS + Dex treatment, Pol 2 largely remains near the TSS resembling a 'paused' pattern seen in the unstimulated BMDM (Figure 2A, left).
evidence: The claim is supported by Pol 2 ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 2A

claim: Non-paused genes Il1a, Il1b and Cd83 display no substantial Pol 2 occupancy in unstimulated BMDM
source: In contrast, non-paused genes Il1a, Il1b and Cd83 display no substantial Pol 2 occupancy in the unstimulated BMDM
evidence: The claim is supported by Pol 2 ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 2A

claim: Non-paused genes Il1a, Il1b and Cd83 show dramatic and uniform increase in Pol 2 occupancy throughout the gene in response to LPS
source: and a dramatic and uniform increase in Pol 2 occupancy throughout the gene in response to LPS
evidence: The claim is supported by Pol 2 ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 2A

claim: At non-paused genes Il1a, Il1b and Cd83, LPS-induced Pol 2 occupancy is nearly abrogated by co-treatment with Dex
source: which is nearly abrogated by co-treatment with Dex (Figure 2A, right).
evidence: The claim is supported by Pol 2 ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 2A

claim: 61 transcripts corresponding to LPS-induced Dex-repressed genes had a PI >1 and were considered to be paused
source: Based on the PI in untreated BMDM, we classified GC-repressed genes into two groups: 61 transcripts had a PI >1 and were considered to be paused (twice as much of Pol2 at the promoter region versus gene body)
evidence: The claim is supported by Pol 2 pausing index calculation from ChIP-seq data

claim: 82 transcripts corresponding to LPS-induced Dex-repressed genes had a PI <0.8 and were considered non-paused
source: whereas 82 had a PI <0.8 and were considered non-paused (see Materials and methods and [Nechaev et al., 2010]).
evidence: The claim is supported by Pol 2 pausing index calculation from ChIP-seq data

claim: At paused genes, LPS treatment causes additional Pol 2 loading and entry into gene bodies
source: The read density distribution for 61 paused and 82 non-paused transcripts in differentially treated BMDM (Figure 2D) reveals a peak of Pol 2 occupancy in the promoters of the paused genes, additional Pol 2 loading, and, importantly, its entry into gene bodies in response to LPS.
evidence: The claim is supported by Pol 2 ChIP-seq read density analysis shown in Figure 2D

claim: Co-treatment with Dex decreases Pol 2 occupancy in gene body of paused genes with most Pol 2 remaining near the TSS
source: Co-treatment with Dex decreases Pol 2 occupancy in gene body with most Pol 2 remaining near the TSS (Figure 2C and D).
evidence: The claim is supported by Pol 2 ChIP-seq data shown in Figures 2C and 2D

claim: Little Pol 2 is seen in non-paused genes in untreated BMDM
source: Conversely, little Pol 2 is seen in the non-paused genes in untreated BMDM
evidence: The claim is supported by Pol 2 ChIP-seq data shown in Figures 2C and 2D

claim: Pol 2 occupancy at non-paused genes increases dramatically throughout the genes in LPS-treated BMDM
source: Pol 2 occupancy increases dramatically throughout the genes in LPS-treated BMDM
evidence: The claim is supported by Pol 2 ChIP-seq data shown in Figures 2C and 2D

claim: LPS-induced Pol 2 loading at non-paused genes is largely abrogated by Dex
source: and this loading is largely abrogated by Dex (Figure 2C and D)
evidence: The claim is supported by Pol 2 ChIP-seq data shown in Figures 2C and 2D

claim: Pol 2 pausing within the first 100 nt of a gene is mediated by NELF
source: Because Pol 2 pausing within the first 100 nt of a gene is mediated by NELF (Adelman and Lis, 2012)
evidence: The claim is supported by established scientific knowledge cited from the literature

claim: NELF-E occupancy matches closely Pol 2 distribution in untreated BMDM with striking accumulation immediately downstream of TSS of paused genes
source: Aligned with Pol 2 PI heat maps, NELF-E occupancy matched closely Pol 2 distribution in untreated BMDM with striking accumulation immediately downstream of TSS of paused genes
evidence: The claim is supported by NELF-E ChIP-seq data shown in Figures 2C and 2D

claim: Little to no NELF-E is seen in non-paused genes in untreated BMDM
source: and little to no NELF-E seen in non-paused genes (Figure 2C and D, far right).
evidence: The claim is supported by NELF-E ChIP-seq data shown in Figures 2C and 2D

claim: Read density distribution in NELF-E ChIP-seq shows highly gene class-specific NELF-E occupancy at paused (PI >1) promoters
source: Indeed, read density distribution in NELF-E ChIP-seq shows highly gene class-specific NELF-E occupancy at paused (PI >1) promoters (Figure 2D, right).
evidence: The claim is supported by NELF-E ChIP-seq read density analysis shown in Figure 2D

claim: Following LPS stimulation, NELF-E is broadly evicted from promoters of LPS-induced genes with little occupancy detected at 1 hr
source: As reported previously for a few individual genes (Adelman et al., 2009; Schaukowitch et al., 2014), following LPS stimulation, NELF-E was broadly evicted from promoters of LPS-induced genes with little occupancy detected at 1 hr (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by NELF-E ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 3A and previous publications

claim: NELF dismissal following LPS stimulation is transient, as NELF reloads onto promoters reaching widespread occupancy by 3 hr despite continued LPS exposure
source: Interestingly, however, this dismissal was transient, as despite continued LPS exposure, NELF reloaded onto promoters reaching widespread occupancy by 3 hr (Figure 3A, also see average occupancy graphed for all paused transcripts).
evidence: The claim is supported by NELF-E ChIP-seq time course data shown in Figure 3A

claim: Paused GC-sensitive genes Tnf, Hilpda, and Btg2 show substantial NELF-E occupancy at the TSS co-localizing with Pol 2 peaks in resting BMDM
source: This release and reloading can be seen at specific paused GC-sensitive genes, Tnf, Hilpda, and Btg2 (Figure 3A, right), which show substantial NELF-E occupancy at the TSS co-localizing with Pol 2 peaks in resting BMDM
evidence: The claim is supported by NELF-E and Pol 2 ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 3A

claim: At Tnf, Hilpda, and Btg2, NELF-E dissociates following a 1 hr LPS induction
source: its dissociation following a 1 hr LPS induction
evidence: The claim is supported by NELF-E ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 3A

claim: At Tnf, Hilpda, and Btg2, TSS-associated NELF-E peaks are re-established by 3 hr of LPS treatment
source: and re-establishment of the TSS-associated NELF-E peaks by 3 hr.
evidence: The claim is supported by NELF-E ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 3A

claim: Among LPS-induced Dex-sensitive genes with PI <0.8, only 31.7% display promoter-associated NELF-E peaks in unstimulated BMDM
source: compared to only 31.7% in genes with PI <0.8 (which comprised approximately 66% of 300 transcripts; Figure 3B, left).
evidence: The claim is supported by NELF-E ChIP-seq peak analysis shown in Figure 3B

claim: Among LPS-induced Dex-insensitive genes, 23% are paused and 70% are non-paused
source: Importantly, similar relative numbers of paused and non-paused genes (23% and 70%, respectively; Figure 3—figure supplement 1B) were found among LPS-induced Dex-insensitive genes from RNA-seq (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by pausing index analysis of Dex-insensitive genes shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B

claim: Among LPS-induced Dex-insensitive genes, NELF-E occupancy in untreated BMDM is more prevalent in paused genes (81.1%) than in non-paused ones (44.2%)
source: In this group, NELF-E occupancy in untreated BMDM was again much more prevalent in paused genes (81.1%) than in non-paused ones (44.2%).
evidence: The claim is supported by NELF-E ChIP-seq analysis of Dex-insensitive genes shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B

claim: GR does not preferentially repress genes in one class (paused vs non-paused) vs. the other
source: Thus, GR does not preferentially repress genes in one class vs. the other
evidence: The claim is inferred from the similar distribution of paused and non-paused genes among Dex-sensitive and Dex-insensitive genes

claim: High levels of TSS-associated NELF in a basal state is a common feature of paused genes irrespective of their sensitivity to GC
source: and high levels of TSS-associated NELF in a basal state is a common feature of paused genes irrespective of their sensitivity to GC.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that both Dex-sensitive and Dex-insensitive paused genes show high NELF occupancy

claim: The relative distribution of NELF-E peaks among paused (PI >1) and non-paused (PI <0.8) repressed genes in LPS+Dex treated BMDM is indistinguishable from NELF-E distribution in resting BMDM
source: We first evaluated NELF-E occupancy in BMDM co-treated with LPS + Dex by ChIP-seq and found the relative distribution of peaks among paused (PI >1) and non-paused (PI <0.8) repressed genes to be indistinguishable from NELF-E distribution in resting BMDM (83.6% and 33.2%, respectively; Figure 3B, right – compare to left).
evidence: The claim is supported by NELF-E ChIP-seq analysis comparing untreated and LPS+Dex conditions shown in Figure 3B

claim: Under LPS + Dex conditions, striking promoter-proximal NELF peaks are detected in paused genes Tnf, Myc, Errfi1 and Ccl2
source: We then evaluated NELF-E distribution across several of our target genes in the presence of LPS + Dex and detected striking promoter-proximal NELF peaks in paused Tnf, Myc, Errfi1 and Ccl2
evidence: The claim is supported by NELF-E ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 3B

claim: Under LPS + Dex conditions, no promoter-proximal NELF peaks are detected in non-paused genes Il1b or Lif
source: but not in non-paused Il1b or Lif (Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by NELF-E ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 3B

claim: BMDM from NELF-B LysM-Cre mice (NELF-B KO) show a dramatic reduction in NELF-B mRNA and protein
source: BMDM from NELF-B LysM-Cre mice (NELF-B KO) show a dramatic reduction in NELF-B mRNA and protein (Figure 3C, top).
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR and western blot data shown in Figure 3C

claim: Loss of a single NELF subunit leads to the proteolytic degradation of the NELF complex
source: Importantly, as the NELF complex requires all four subunits for stability and the loss of a single subunit leads to the proteolytic degradation of the complex (Gilchrist et al., 2008)
evidence: The claim is supported by established knowledge from the cited literature

claim: BMDM of NELF-B KO mice show a near complete loss of the NELF-E protein
source: immunoblot also reveals a near complete loss of the NELF-E protein in the BMDM of the NELF-B KO (Figure 3C, top).
evidence: The claim is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 3C

claim: RNA-seq of resting BMDM from WT and NELF-B KO mice reveals no significant differences in the expression levels of LPS-induced Dex-repressed genes at baseline
source: Consistent with the lack of overt phenotype in these mice, RNA-seq of resting BMDM of the two genotypes revealed no significant differences in the expression levels of LPS-induced Dex-repressed genes at baseline (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C

claim: LPS challenge leads to similar induction of Tnf, Myc, Errfi1, Ccl2, Il1b and Lif transcripts in WT and NELF-B KO BMDM
source: Moreover, at the time-frame examined, LPS challenge led to a similar induction of Tnf, Myc, Errfi1, Ccl2, Il1b and Lif transcripts irrespective of the genotype (Figure 3C, bottom left).
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 3C

claim: For all genes classified as 'paused', repression by Dex is significantly attenuated in the NELF-B KO BMDM
source: Interestingly, for all genes classified as 'paused', repression by Dex was significantly attenuated in the NELF-B KO BMDM
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data comparing Dex repression in WT vs NELF-B KO BMDM shown in Figure 3C

claim: For non-paused genes Il1b and Lif, repression by Dex is not attenuated in NELF-B KO BMDM
source: but not in non-paused genes Il1b and Lif (Figure 3C, bottom right).
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 3C

claim: NELF-mediated block in productive elongation is an integral part of GR-mediated repression of paused genes
source: Collectively, these findings strongly suggest that NELF-mediated block in productive elongation is an integral part of GR-mediated repression of paused genes.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the genetic evidence showing NELF requirement for GR repression of paused genes

claim: Out of 201 genes repressed by Dex in WT BMDM, 23 are expressed at higher level in LPS + Dex-treated NELF-B KO BMDM
source: Out of 201 genes that were repressed by Dex in the WT BMDM (Figure 1A), 23 were expressed at higher level in the LPS + Dex-treated NELF-B KO BMDM
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq analysis comparing WT and NELF-B KO BMDM shown in Figure 3D

claim: Of 23 Dex-repressed genes upregulated in NELF-B KO BMDM under LPS+Dex conditions, 21 had PI >0.8
source: notably, 21 of them had PI >0.8 (Figure 3D).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq and pausing index analysis shown in Figure 3D

claim: Out of 396 LPS-induced Dex-insensitive genes, only nine are upregulated in LPS + Dex-treated NELF-B KO BMDM
source: Conversely, out of 396 LPS-induced Dex-insensitive genes, only nine were upregulated in the LPS + Dex-treated NELF-B KO BMDM
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D

claim: Of 9 Dex-insensitive genes upregulated in NELF-B KO BMDM under LPS+Dex conditions, 7 had PI >0.8
source: 7 of which had PI >0.8 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D, left).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq and pausing index analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D

claim: NELF ablation disproportionally affects paused LPS-induced Dex-repressed genes
source: These observations indicate that NELF ablation disproportionally affects paused LPS-induced Dex-repressed genes.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the RNA-seq analysis showing preferential derepression of paused genes in NELF-B KO

claim: GR inhibits LPS-induced CDK9 recruitment irrespective of gene class
source: Consistent with earlier observations (Luecke and Yamamoto, 2005), GR inhibited LPS-induced CDK9 recruitment but did so irrespective of the gene class (Figure 3E)
evidence: The claim is supported by CDK9 ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 3E and previous publications

claim: NELF retention rather than CDK9 occupancy serves as a defining class-specific feature of glucocorticoid repression of paused genes
source: suggesting that NELF retention rather than CDK9 occupancy serves as a defining class-specific feature of glucocorticoid repression of paused genes.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that CDK9 loss is not gene class-specific while NELF retention is

claim: Paused genes Tnf and Ccl2 contain high basal levels of H4PanAc and H4K5Ac at both TSS and kB-binding sites
source: In particular, paused genes - Tnf and Ccl2 - contained high basal levels of H4PanAc and, specifically, H4K5Ac, at both TSS- and kB-binding sites
evidence: The claim is supported by histone acetylation ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 4A

claim: At paused genes Tnf and Ccl2, H4Ac levels are unaffected by LPS or LPS + Dex treatment
source: which were unaffected by LPS or LPS + Dex treatment (Figure 4A, bottom row).
evidence: The claim is supported by histone acetylation ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 4A

claim: Non-paused genes Il1b and Il1a show a significant increase in H4Ac levels only after LPS treatment
source: In contrast, non-paused genes - Il1b and Il1a - showed a significant increase in H4Ac levels only after LPS treatment
evidence: The claim is supported by histone acetylation ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 4A

claim: At non-paused genes Il1b and Il1a, LPS-induced increase in H4Ac is fully attenuated by Dex
source: and this increase was fully attenuated by Dex (Figure 4A, top row).
evidence: The claim is supported by histone acetylation ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 4A

claim: I-BET attenuates LPS-mediated induction of Il1b and Il1a transcripts in a dose-dependent manner
source: The induction of Il1b and Il1a transcripts was significantly attenuated by I-BET in a dose-dependent manner

claim: Tnf and Ccl2 induction persists in the presence of I-BET
source: whereas Tnf and Ccl2 induction persisted (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is supported by RT-qPCR data from I-BET inhibitor experiments shown in Figure 4B

claim: BRD4 is recruited to promoters of non-paused genes Il1b and Il1a upon LPS treatment
source: In agreement with gene expression results, ChIP-qPCR experiments revealed that BRD4 was recruited to promoters of non-paused genes Il1b and Il1a upon LPS treatment
evidence: The claim is supported by BRD4 ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 4C

claim: LPS-induced BRD4 recruitment to Il1b and Il1a promoters is attenuated by Dex
source: and, interestingly, this recruitment was attenuated by Dex (Figure 4C).
evidence: The claim is supported by BRD4 ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 4C

claim: At paused genes Tnf and Ccl2, BRD4 is readily detectable at the TSS in unstimulated BMDM
source: Conversely, at the paused genes, Tnf and Ccl2, BRD4 was readily detectable at the TSS in unstimulated BMDM
evidence: The claim is supported by BRD4 ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 4C

claim: At paused genes Tnf and Ccl2, BRD4 association does not significantly change after LPS or LPS + Dex treatment
source: and this association did not significantly change after either LPS or LPS + Dex treatment.
evidence: The claim is supported by BRD4 ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 4C

claim: BRD4 occupancy patterns at promoters resemble signal-responsive H4Ac profiles
source: Thus, BRD4 occupancy patterns at the promoters of these genes resembled signal-responsive H4Ac profiles
evidence: The claim is inferred from comparing BRD4 and H4Ac ChIP data

claim: Loss of BRD4 in response to Dex may underlie GR-mediated repression of specifically the non-paused genes
source: suggesting that loss of BRD4 in response to Dex may underlie GR-mediated repression of, specifically, the non-paused genes.
evidence: The claim is speculated based on the correlation between BRD4 loss and gene repression at non-paused genes

claim: Approximately 3700 BRD4 peaks are observed across the genome in untreated BMDM
source: Not surprisingly, we observed frequent BRD4 binding across the genome in untreated BMDM (~3700 peaks, Figure 4—figure supplement 1A, left panel).
